cards.text: Moses has been up on Mount Sinai with God, and he's delayed in coming down. So the people crowd around Aaron, Moses' brother, and say they don't know what's happened to Moses. It's like the app says your package is "arriving today," and by dinner the whole house has declared it gone FOREVER.

cards.question: So what do the people ask Aaron to make for them?

answers.text: Gods who will go before them

cards.question: Aaron tells the people to take something off their wives and sons and daughters and bring it to him. What is it?
Only some of the people take off their gold earrings and bring them to Aaron.

cards.text: Aaron takes the gold from their hands. He picks up an engraving tool and gets to work.

cards.question: Aaron takes the people's gold and fashions it into a molten ___.
The people look at the calf Aaron made and say something about it. What do they say?

answers.text: These are your gods who brought you out of Egypt
This will lead us into the land God promised
This will keep us safe until Moses returns

cards.text: That calf came out of their OWN earrings, and now Aaron builds an altar in front of it and announces a feast for tomorrow. That's like me stamping a cookie and then thanking the cookie for stamping ME.

cards.question: Aaron proclaims a feast for tomorrow. Who does he say the feast is to?

cards.text: So the next day they get up and offer burnt offerings and peace offerings.

cards.question: After the burnt offerings and peace offerings, what do the people do?

answers.text: Eat and drink and party wildly

cards.text: Meanwhile, up on the mountain, the LORD speaks to Moses. He says, "Go down at once, for your people, whom you brought up out of the land of Egypt, have corrupted themselves."

cards.question: The LORD says the people were slow to turn aside from the way He commanded them.

cards.text: The LORD also says He has seen this people, and they are indeed a stiff-necked people. That's dough straight out of the freezer, friend, and I have leaned my WHOLE mustache on it and it will not roll.

cards.question: The LORD tells Moses to leave Him alone so His anger may burn against the people. Then, He says, He will make Moses into a great ___.

cards.text: A whole nation, just from Moses, and he doesn't even reach for it. Instead, Moses seeks the favor of the LORD his God.

cards.question: Moses asks the LORD why His anger should burn against His people. What does Moses say the Egyptians would declare?

answers.text: He brought them out to kill them in the mountains
Their own gods had beaten the God of Israel
Moses tricked the people into leaving Egypt

cards.question: Moses asks the LORD to remember His servants ___ and Isaac and ___, and the promise He swore to them of descendants and land.
After Moses pleads, the LORD relents from the calamity He had threatened to bring on His people.

cards.text: Moses turns and heads down the mountain with the two tablets of the Testimony in his hands, inscribed on both sides, front and back. Friend, these tablets are the work of God, and the writing is the writing of God, engraved right on them.
On the way down, Joshua, Moses' assistant, hears the people shouting, and his ears go straight to trouble. He tells Moses, "The sound of war is in the camp."

cards.question: Moses hears the same shouting from the camp. What does he say it is?

cards.text: Moses gets close enough to SEE it: the calf, and the dancing. And Moses burns with anger.

cards.question: Moses hands the tablets to Joshua for safekeeping.
Moses throws the tablets, and they shatter at the base of the mountain. Then he burns the calf, grinds it to powder, scatters it over the water and makes the Israelites ___ it.

cards.text: Then Moses turns to Aaron, and friend, I would NOT want to be in Aaron's apron right now. Moses asks what this people did to him that he would lead them into so great a sin.

cards.question: Aaron tells Moses not to be enraged. Then what does Aaron say about the people?

answers.text: They only meant to honor Moses

cards.question: Aaron repeats what the people asked for and says he told whoever had gold to take it off. What does he say happened when he threw the gold into the fire?

cards.text: Out came this calf? That's me telling you the dough stamped ITSELF, with flour still all over my mustache. Moses sees the people are out of control, for Aaron had let them run wild, and they've become a laughingstock to their enemies.

cards.question: Moses stands at the entrance to the camp and calls out, "Whoever is for the LORD, come to me." Who gathers around him?

cards.text: This next part is heavy, friend. Moses gives them a command from the LORD, the God of Israel: each man is to fasten his sword to his side, go through the camp from gate to gate, and slay his brother, his friend and his neighbor.

cards.question: The Levites do as Moses commanded, and about three thousand of the people fall dead that day.

cards.text: Moses tells the Levites they've been ordained for service to the LORD today. And after ALL that, Moses still isn't giving up on the people: the next day he tells them they've committed a great sin, but he'll go up to the LORD, because perhaps he can make atonement for their sin.

cards.question: Moses goes back to the LORD and asks Him to forgive the people's sin. But if not, what does Moses ask for?

answers.text: To be blotted out of God's book
To be released from leading them
To be given a new people to lead

cards.question: The LORD replies that whoever has ___ against Him, He will blot out of His book.
The LORD tells Moses to stay on the mountain while the people wait at the camp.

cards.text: The LORD says His angel will go before them. But on the day He settles accounts, He will punish them for their sin.
And the LORD sends a plague on the people because of what they did with the calf Aaron made. We'll pause the oven right there, friend, because this story isn't over.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: 'Out came this calf?', the dough joke, and the verse 25 sentence. It also carries two beats, the reaction to Aaron's excuse (v24) and Moses seeing the people out of control (v25).

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The card opens by echoing Aaron's line from verse 24 ('Out came this calf?') but cites only Exodus 32:25. It should cite Exodus 32:24-25.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The first sentence retells the promise from verse 10 ('A whole nation, just from Moses') but the card cites only Exodus 32:11. It should cite Exodus 32:10-11.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The card states that the calf came out of the people's own earrings (Exodus 32:2-4) but cites only Exodus 32:5. It should cite Exodus 32:2-5.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: Multiple choice dominates both stops. Stop 1 has 6 multiple choice, 3 true or false and 3 fill in the blank. Stop 2 has 5 multiple choice, 3 true or false and 2 fill in the blank.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: Some story cards state facts from outside the passage: 'Mount Sinai' and 'Aaron, Moses' brother' (stop 1, card 1), and 'Joshua, Moses' assistant' (stop 2, card 2). Their cited verses are only from Exodus 32, so these facts carry no reference. The docs require a reference for every Bible fact and allow outside facts 'with their reference.' They don't say how to record an outside reference in a card's verses field, which uses a single passage range.
findings.question: When a story card introduces a person or place with a fact from outside the passage (like Ex 4:14 for Aaron or Ex 24:13 for Joshua), should that outside reference go in the card's verses field, go somewhere else, or be left off?
